Artistic Concept: "The Breath of the Andes"

This concept envisions a multimedia narrative installation that immerses the viewer in the spiritual and physical landscape of the Quechua people. The visual centerpiece is a large-scale, textured tapestry woven with natural fibers, depicting the rugged peaks of the Andes not just as geography, but as living ancestors. Interspersed within the weave are subtle, glowing threads representing the connection to Pachamama (Mother Earth), symbolizing the deep spirituality that grounds daily life.

The soundscape features the rhythmic beating of traditional drums and the wind whistling through high-altitude valleys, creating an atmosphere of both struggle and serene beauty. Interactive elements allow visitors to place their hands on specific sections of the tapestry, triggering audio clips of Quechua poetry and stories that highlight the resilience and dignity of indigenous communities. The lighting shifts from the cool blues of dawn to the warm golds of midday, mirroring the cycle of labor and rest. This installation aims to honor the origins of the Quechua culture by focusing on their enduring relationship with the land, moving beyond stereotypes to present a nuanced, respectful portrayal of their traditions and spiritual depth.

Regarding the priority question: The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.
